stories.title: Delhi launches mental health policy for schools
stories.summary: The Delhi government has introduced the Ehsaas 2026 policy, aiming to provide one counsellor for every 500 students in educational institutions. The initiative includes new helplines and emotional support services. The policy seeks to encourage students, teachers, and parents to speak openly about mental health.

stories.title: Delhi government unveils mental well-being policy
stories.summary: The Delhi government has launched a mental well-being policy for children and youth. Education Minister Ashish Sood stated the initiative follows concerns regarding student support and a recent suicide attempt by a school student. The policy aims to address the emotional and psychological health of young people.

stories.title: Delhi launches Ehsaas 2026 mental health initiative
stories.summary: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has launched the capital's first Mental Health and Well-being Policy, titled Ehsaas 2026. The program aims to support over 45 lakh students through dedicated counselling, a 24-hour mental health helpline, and emotional support services.

stories.title: Michigan lawmakers propose using social media settlement funds for youth mental health
stories.summary: Michigan is receiving $171 million from a federal settlement with Meta over allegations of addictive platform features. Two state lawmakers have introduced bills to direct these funds toward youth mental health. Where the settlement money will be spent remains currently unclear.

stories.title: Lawmakers renew push for Mental Health Justice Act
stories.summary: A group of 46 lawmakers has reintroduced the Mental Health Justice Act to reduce violence against individuals with mental health conditions and disabilities. The bill proposes federal grants for local governments to dispatch mental health professionals instead of police when responding to 911 or 988 calls.

stories.title: Detroit receives $12 million grant for mental health and housing
stories.summary: The Detroit Health Department has been awarded a $12 million federal grant to support residents experiencing homelessness. The funding, provided through the PATHS initiative, will assist more than 2,100 people with mental health care, substance use treatment, and housing support over the next four years.

stories.title: Climate change impacts mental health of young people in Colombia
stories.summary: A study of young people in Colombia’s Aburrá Valley found that environmental degradation is causing widespread feelings of sadness, fear, and guilt. While 90% of those surveyed expressed a desire to take action, many report that climate change has taken a toll on their mental health.

stories.title: Kate Spade prioritizes mental health initiatives
stories.summary: Kate Spade has announced a mission to prioritize mental health for staff and women globally. The brand aims to reach 250,000 individuals as part of its social impact strategy. The company says it is focusing on tangible impact to avoid what it describes as green and blue washing.

stories.title: Caterpillar worker sues over termination after mental health day request
stories.summary: A former Caterpillar employee has filed a federal lawsuit alleging disability discrimination and retaliation. The complaint claims the company fired him the same day he requested a mental health day, subsequently accusing him of threatening colleagues. Caterpillar has not commented on the specific allegations.

stories.title: Texas ranks among top 10 states for anxiety and depression - CW33.com
Punjab begins teacher training on student mental health
stories.summary: Punjab has launched a phased training program for over 21,850 teachers to help identify early signs of student mental health concerns and substance use. The initiative is part of the state's anti-drug campaign, with workshops already underway in Fazilka and Tarn Taran districts.

stories.title: Temple University reviews sexual assault response
stories.summary: A new university committee is reviewing how Temple University handles reports of sexual assault. Separately, Mother Bethel AME Church is offering free mental health first aid training for Philadelphia residents, covering how to assist neighbors or friends who may be experiencing a mental health crisis.

stories.title: Students turn to meditation to manage academic stress
stories.summary: More than 60 students participated in a workshop at the University of Science in Ho Chi Minh City to practice breathing meditation. The event aimed to help participants balance their minds amidst the pressures of study and urban life by choosing to sit still.

stories.title: Backdrop of Belfast provides the space for breathwork - ITVX
Research explores the physiology of gratitude
stories.summary: Recent scientific studies suggest gratitude provides significant benefits for mental and physical health. Researchers are now working to map the brain's response to the emotion. Understanding the physiology of gratitude could help experts develop new strategies for harnessing its health benefits.

stories.title: Grocery stores as sites of social civility
stories.summary: The grocery store is described as an oasis of civility during politically divisive times. Observations of shoppers navigating aisles and checkout lines suggest that people from diverse backgrounds can maintain orderly behavior in shared public spaces, even when minor accidents occur.

stories.title: Design framework developed for anxiety-friendly public art
stories.summary: Researchers have created a design framework to help urban planners translate the needs of adults with mild anxiety into digital public art. The study aims to reduce sensory disruptions in shared spaces, addressing a gap in how psychological needs are integrated into public art specifications.

stories.title: Naming emotions as a strategy for mental health
stories.summary: Dr. David Kimhy of the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai suggests that precisely naming emotions can improve emotional regulation. He notes that identifying specific feelings like anger or guilt allows for more effective coping strategies than simply feeling bad.

stories.title: Intensive retreat linked to temporary gene expression changes
stories.summary: A study of 106 individuals found that an eight-day silent residential retreat caused widespread but temporary alterations in gene expression related to stress and antiviral defenses. Researchers assessed blood samples across four timepoints, noting shifts in transcriptional signatures without significant changes to overall immune cell counts.

stories.title: Uganda Study Finds Group Therapy Reduces Depression Symptoms Among Participants - AfricaBrief
Puppies and yoga studio opens in Santa Ana
stories.summary: A new studio in downtown Santa Ana offers a 75-minute session combining beginner-friendly yoga with 30 minutes of puppy interaction. The company provides mats and requires no prior experience, relying on the appeal of puppies aged eight to twelve weeks to roam the studio during the practice.

stories.title: High-intensity yoga identified as top sleep aid
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 30 randomized controlled trials published in Sleep and Biological Rhythms compared various exercise forms for sleep improvement. Researchers at Harbin Sport University identified high-intensity yoga as the most effective workout for tackling sleep disruption among the methods studied.

stories.title: Consistency in exercise linked to mental well-being
stories.summary: A study of more than 10,000 college students suggests that exercise frequency may be more important for mental health than workout intensity. Students who exercised less frequently were more likely to report depression and anxiety a year later, indicating that consistency is a key factor.

stories.title: Electroacupuncture shows potential in preclinical insomnia study
stories.summary: Researchers found that stimulating specific acupoints in mice using alternating 2 Hz and 100 Hz electrical frequencies reduced sleep latency and normalized brain neurotransmitters. The preclinical study, published in Innovations in Acupuncture and Medicine, suggests these frequencies may help mitigate chemically induced insomnia symptoms.

stories.title: Study finds high suicide risk among nursing students in Bangladesh
stories.summary: A cross-sectional investigation across five nursing institutions in Bangladesh found that nearly 16 percent of students surveyed were at high risk for suicidal behavior. The study highlights the emotional strain of clinical rotations and coursework, noting that systematic evaluations of these cohorts had previously been limited.

stories.title: Stress management tips for immediate relief
stories.summary: Everyday Health suggests that while restorative practices like yoga are beneficial for long-term stress, they may not address immediate triggers like missed flights or workplace emails. The publication offers five quick strategies to manage physiological stress responses such as racing hearts and sweaty palms.

stories.title: Author discusses mental health and holiday silence
stories.summary: Ray Greenstreet, author of Below the Breaking Point, suggests that silence is a primary challenge for mental health. He discussed his perspective on protecting well-being ahead of the holiday season during a recent media appearance.

stories.title: Hospital offers mental health tips for holiday stress
stories.summary: Forest View Hospital suggests that holiday preparations like cooking, travel, and shopping can lead to overwhelm. The hospital recommends practical management strategies and seeking professional help when holiday interactions or dinner conversations exacerbate existing mental health concerns.

stories.title: Cardiologist notes cold weather heart risks
stories.summary: A cardiologist explains that cold mornings may increase the risk of heart attacks. The report outlines necessary precautions for maintaining heart health during winter months, emphasizing the physiological impact of temperature changes on the cardiovascular system.

stories.title: Broadcaster credits short kettlebell workouts for strength
stories.summary: Broadcaster Mariella Frostrup says she maintains strength by performing 15-minute kettlebell workouts found on YouTube. While she notes the sessions can be physically taxing, she maintains that short, frequent routines are sufficient for her personal fitness goals.

stories.title: Actor discusses daily exercise routine
stories.summary: Emmerdale actor Natalie J. Robb says she maintains an intense daily exercise routine to support her physical and mental health. She notes that the demands of learning lines and a busy filming schedule make regular physical activity a necessary part of her wind-down process.

stories.title: Presenter shares core strength routine
stories.summary: Presenter Jenny Powell says she uses light dumbbells and yoga to maintain strength. She credits her regular practice with helping her manage anxiety and the physical changes associated with menopause, noting that heavy weights are not required for her routine.

stories.title: Hotpod Yoga updates class structure
stories.summary: Hotpod Yoga has reorganized its class offerings into six formats focused on strength, recovery, and mobility. The brand, which operates over 65 studios, continues to use its signature purpose-built heated pods to provide a dimly lit environment for its sessions.

stories.title: Explosive strength training for hiking
stories.summary: Training for steep inclines requires explosive strength, which allows hikers to quickly muster force during strides. Experts note that walking up a 5 percent incline burns roughly 44 percent more calories per hour than flat ground, making power-focused training a key factor in uphill performance.

stories.title: Jennifer Lopez attributes strength gains to weight training
stories.summary: Jennifer Lopez says that incorporating weight training into her fitness routine roughly a decade ago changed her approach to exercise. The 57-year-old actor says focusing on the muscle component of her workouts has been essential for staving off age-related muscle loss.

stories.title: Cheryl Tiegs on staying active
stories.summary: Cheryl Tiegs, dubbed America's first supermodel, says she maintains her wellbeing by listening to her body and avoiding discomfort during exercise. The 79-year-old prioritises walking and hiking to stay active. She hopes to remain as healthy in 20 years as she is today.

stories.title: Strength training and depression
stories.summary: A study in JAMA Network Open suggests resistance training may help ease symptoms of depression. Experts note that lifting weights provides concrete, measurable progress that can boost confidence. The research found that the benefits of resistance training over cardio were small, but noticeable.

stories.title: AJ Odudu on training for survival
stories.summary: TV presenter AJ Odudu says she relies on bodyweight exercises like push-ups and squats to build strength. Before appearing on a reality show, she expressed optimism that her training would be useful, though she noted uncertainty about how pull-ups prepare one for being covered in cockroaches.

stories.title: Keto diet and liver fat
stories.summary: A clinical trial published by Cell Press found that a ketogenic diet reduced liver fat by an average of 67 percent in four months. The diet outperformed Mediterranean and low-fat alternatives in improving metabolic health, with half of participants no longer meeting criteria for prediabetes.

stories.title: Junk food and memory recovery
stories.summary: A review of rodent experiments in Nutritional Neuroscience suggests that switching from a junk food diet to healthy food may help recover some lost memory. The study noted that memory gains were observed with high-fat diets, though all findings are limited to rodents.

Wellness cafe opens in Bengaluru
stories.summary: La Verde Cafe has opened in Bengaluru inside the Ignite + Aliign fitness studio. The venue focuses on functional beverages and superfoods. Founded by actress Shubra Aiyappa and yoga practitioners, the space features an open design intended to encourage mindful eating and hydration.

stories.title: Breakfast and blood sugar
Longevity tracking in grocery stores
stories.summary: The Food Institute reports that consumers are increasingly using biometrics and nutrition to influence their healthspan. Supplement brand co-founder Sam Naish says that wearables and health podcasts have turned biological age into a daily focus, changing how shoppers view their grocery purchases.

stories.title: Are Your Plant-Based Meat Alternatives Hiding Fungal Toxins? - Men's Journal
Healthspan versus life expectancy
stories.summary: A 2026 Global Burden of Disease analysis found that Americans spend an average of 14 years in poor health. While life expectancy rose by six months between 2009 and 2019, healthy life expectancy fell. Biological age is now used as an estimate of physical health.

stories.title: Manulife launches longevity training program - Advisor.ca
Cellular health and aging
stories.summary: The beauty industry is shifting its focus toward longevity and cellular function rather than just appearance. Companies like Timeline are marketing products aimed at the muscles and cellular processes that keep bodies functioning as they age, moving beyond traditional skin care routines.

stories.title: Nearly half of adults over 70 benefited from exercise training across several areas of physical function - Medical Xpres
Reading linked to lower dementia risk
stories.summary: Research from the University of Cambridge suggests reading for pleasure is associated with a 33 percent lower risk of Alzheimer's disease. Studies also indicate that five minutes of fiction can reduce stress by up to 20 percent. The habit is linked to better memory.

stories.title: Longevity and body composition
stories.summary: Fitness operators are increasingly using body composition data to market longevity services. By tracking muscle health and metabolic resilience, companies like seca aim to provide medically validated insights into long-term performance. The focus is on making healthy aging a measurable process.

stories.title: Calf size and longevity
stories.summary: A 2022 systematic review found that for every 1 cm increase in calf circumference, a person's risk of death fell by an average of 5 percent. Physical therapist Kara McKeown notes that while muscle mass predicts longevity, it does not necessarily require extreme lower-body training.

stories.title: Loneliness linked to faster biological aging
stories.summary: A new study in Health Psychology suggests loneliness and social isolation are linked to faster biological aging. Each point on the isolation scale correlated with a nearly 14 percent higher risk of death. The study notes it cannot prove social connection slows aging or prevents death.

stories.title: South Korea life expectancy gains shift to older ages
stories.summary: A demographic analysis of South Korean vital statistics from 1970 to 2023 shows a shift in longevity drivers. While early gains resulted from fewer premature deaths, improvements since 2000 are increasingly driven by a rightward shift of the entire age at death distribution.

stories.title: Yoga intervention shows benefits for older inmates
stories.summary: A nine-week yoga program at a German open prison facility reportedly improved mental well-being and social connectedness for eight participants aged 61 to 71. Sports scientists from Bielefeld University conducted the study, which explored how physical activity addresses the strains of aging while incarcerated.

stories.title: Brain interfaces measure acupuncture signals without clinical proof
stories.summary: A review of 63 studies indicates that brain-computer interfaces can reliably measure neural activity during acupuncture. However, researchers found no clinical evidence that real-time, brain-guided adjustments improve patient outcomes compared to standardized care. Laboratory observation remains distinct from clinical benefit.

stories.title: Knee osteoarthritis affects millions globally
stories.summary: Knee osteoarthritis impacts an estimated 365 million people worldwide, representing the largest share of the 528 million cases of joint disorders. Clinical literature identifies female sex, hypertension, hyperglycemia, obesity, and prior joint injuries as primary risk factors for the condition alongside advanced age.

stories.title: Japanese acupuncturists favor GB20 for migraine treatment
stories.summary: A survey of licensed acupuncturists in Japan found that practitioners frequently select the gall bladder meridian point GB20 for migraine treatment. The study aimed to identify real-world clinical practices rather than relying on textbook prescriptions to help guide the design of future randomized control trials.

stories.title: Acupuncture and stroke treatment show low certainty gains
stories.summary: A systematic review published in Frontiers in Neurology evaluated combining acupuncture with intravenous alteplase for acute ischemic stroke. While the combination may improve clinical response rates, the researchers classified the evidence for these gains as having low certainty. The therapeutic window remains a constraint.

stories.title: Editorial evaluates traditional medicine through biomedical frameworks
stories.summary: An editorial in Innovations in Acupuncture and Medicine synthesizes 20 articles applying genomic and physiological techniques to traditional medical concepts. The authors address scientific inquiry into pattern differentiation and individualized care, moving beyond purely empirical systems to evaluate these practices within modern biomedical frameworks.

stories.title: Ayurveda Day reports millions of digital participants
stories.summary: The 11th Ayurveda Day on September 23 recorded over 13 million registrations on its official digital platform, according to the Ministry of Ayush. The event featured more than 22,000 reported activities globally under the theme of a healthier tomorrow. Digital participation has been documented.

stories.title: Swami Ramdev advocates for traditional lifestyle practices
stories.summary: During Chhath Puja, Swami Ramdev encouraged a return to Ayurveda, Yoga, and ancestral heritage. He described these practices as the foundation of the Indian way of life rather than purely cultural subjects, urging society to align its healthcare and education systems with traditional principles.
